state.case_summary:
A man in his early 70s presented with a 2-year history of a mildly pruritic, erythematous, and gradually enlarging lesion on the proximal portion of his left calf. The lesion had appeared without an identifiable cause. For the previous 2 months, the patient had applied topical corticosteroids and antifungals with no improvement.

Physical examination revealed an ill-defined, nonindurated, erythematous-violaceous plaque that was slightly raised but with an atrophic appearance.

- Histopathology:    - Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone    - Round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells    - No hemosiderin deposits found with Perls Prussian blue stain    - Immunohistochemistry: Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD34 and CD31 but negative for D2-40  Images:    - Figure A Title: Clinical image of the left calf    Description: Ill-defined, erythematous-violaceous plaque with an atrophic appearance        - Figure B Title: Histopathology image    Description: Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with no grenz zone (hematoxylin-eosin)        - Figure C Title: Histopathology image    Description: Round vascular channels lined by a single layer of endothelial cells without atypia (hematoxylin-eosin)        - Figure D Title: Immunohistochemistry image    Description: CD34 immunostaining labels endothelial cells
